analysis:
Reviewed all supplied units.

1) coordinator/tests/api/billing/payouts/global_payouts_queue_test.go (test-only). Head adds f.state = "processing" under the fixture mutex at head line 58, and a ninth syncGlobalPayout call (head lines 66-69) after the concurrent workers. This asserts that a later reconcile-only worker does not submit a second payment (f.creates == 1, head line 76) and does not debit the ledger twice (head line 82). It strengthens coverage of idempotent single-send under concurrent workers and of the persisted retry key "gp-withdraw-<id>-funding-1". No production code is changed. It touches the payment ledger (A-009) and the TB-008 boundary only through test coverage, so there are no regressions or new attack surface.

2) docs/README.md, docs/architecture/README.md. Documentation only: stamp dates updated, and a new link to architecture/kv-cache-quantization.md added. The prefix-cache descriptions were reworded: base said "exact prefix reuse" and "why a default box builds no SSD cache"; head says "compatible prefix reuse" and "default-eligible encrypted SSD caching".

Threat-model note for the next pass: this wording suggests a lossy or quantized checkpoint restore and "compatible" (not exact) prefix reuse. That could touch T-041 (cross-tenant prefix-cache sharing and TTFT oracle, SEC-035) and cache-aware routing's "exact" proof semantics. The actual source for the KV quantization and prefix-cache behavior is not in this batch. The linked kv-cache-quantization.md is not supplied, so I cannot verify any behavior change. If the full PR changes the SSD payload format, lookup tags, scope folding, TTL or the lossy restore path, review those against T-041 mitigations (a)-(e). From this batch alone I cannot conclude a security regression; it is a coverage limit.
